previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fever, dysuria, nausea, and back pain, two days after feeling unwell at home. She had a history of recurrent UTIs, ESBL, and supratherapeutic INR. On admission, she was hypotensive and tachycardic, requiring fluid resuscitation and ICU monitoring. Her INR was 11.1, and she received vitamin K. Urine culture grew ESBL E. coli, leading to a switch from broad-spectrum antibiotics to Bactrim. Her warfarin was held and later restarted at 3 mg daily due to drug interaction risks. She improved clinically, remained afebrile, and was discharged home on a 14-day course of Bactrim, reduced-dose warfarin, and adjusted chronic medications. Daily INR monitoring was arranged. Liver ultrasound showed fatty infiltration; no acute intracranial bleed was found on CT. She was alert at discharge with stable vital signs and no respiratory support needed.

Evaluation is limited due to poor photon penetration.  Within these
limitations, the lungs are well expanded and show mild bilateral interstitial
and focal airspace opacities.  The cardiac silhouette is enlarged.  The
mediastinal silhouette and hilar contours are normal.  More linear opacities
noted in the left mid lung.  No pleural effusions are present.

IMPRESSION:
Mild interstitial edema has now progressed.
